No roadmap of the atlas plans potential theory in the plane or arithmetic rationality criteria; DT.5 (E/G-functions) is the nearest, and André's G-function theory contains the same rationality criteria (the source notes that André's theorem VIII 1.6 can replace Bertrandias's). Ownership under the upstream tier rule (REV-ClassicalArithmeticCompletion\~3): the roadmap LogarithmicPotentialTheoryAndAlgebraicIntegers now exists, and its accepted design packet plans logarithmic capacity and the transfinite diameter in layer LP.1 (LP.1/capacity, LP.1/transfinite-diameter, LP.1/diameter-capacity), but neither Dubinin's hedgehog bound nor Bertrandias's rationality theorem. It is not among the roadmaps that precede this tier-5 roadmap in research/blueprint/upstream/CaraianiNewton.md, so CA.6 does not import from it. The transfinite diameter, Dubinin's bound and Bertrandias's theorem, at the contracts stated here, are CA.6-owned inputs of its continuation; LP.1 imports the capacity notions from CA.6 once they are planned, unless the upstream order is revised to place LogarithmicPotentialTheoryAndAlgebraicIntegers below this roadmap. *Proposal:* Under the upstream tier rule CA.6 owns these three inputs and plans them in its continuation; LogarithmicPotentialTheoryAndAlgebraicIntegers (LP.1, general complex capacity) and the ArithmeticAlgebraizationAndHolonomyBounds direction (arithmetic rationality criteria) import them from CA.6 afterwards. Alternatively the orchestrator may place LogarithmicPotentialTheoryAndAlgebraicIntegers below this roadmap in the upstream order, after which CA.6 imports LP.1's capacity and transfinite diameter instead of planning them. No rescope or new atlas layer is applied by this pass.

CA.7 is kept in this roadmap, as the accepted RS-03 decides, but it is too broad to read as one star: it now has 55 nodes in four coherent groups that share few prerequisites with each other, and none with CA.0–CA.6. Divide it into four sub-layers, each a parent node of the stage. *Proposal:* CA.7a Normal bases, tameness and the trace: ring-of-integers-as-group-ring-module, rational-normal-basis-map, normal-basis-generators-differ-by-units, normal-integral-basis, trace-of-normal-integral-basis-generator, trace-surjective-of-normal-integral-basis, tamely-ramified, trace-modulo-a-prime, prime-divides-trace-ideal-iff-not-tame, tame-iff-trace-surjective, tame-of-normal-integral-basis, gaussian-integers-have-no-normal-integral-basis, rim-projectivity-criterion, projective-of-tame, trace-surjective-of-projective. Projective K₀ already exists in Tau Ceti; only the arithmetic interfaces move down. *Proposal:* ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.7 owns the stable-equivalence/free-complement criterion, balanced scalar extension/restriction on projectives and the K₀/class-group comparison; the Steinitz class and pseudobases are GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.2’s and are imported. Point KTheoryLowDegrees Z.1 and Z.4 at these continuation IDs and at GN.2; retain general higher K-theory and K₁ there.
15. **rescope** (ClassicalArithmeticCompletion, FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums; CA.7 continuation packet). The two finite Gauss inputs required for Taylor cannot be upward dependencies of CA.7. Current Mathlib already owns the sum and elementary identities. *Proposal:* CA.7 owns finite-gauss-valuation and finite-gauss-product as narrow moved-down inputs. FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums FF.1 imports them; it keeps the wider Jacobi-sum and character-sum programme. Do not move the existing Mathlib gaussSum carrier.
16. **split** (ClassicalArithmeticCompletion; CA.7 continuation packet). The retained 55 targets and this continuation give three coherent mathematical blocks within CA.7; this is a proposal under the accepted RS-03 structure, with no atlas edit. *Proposal:* At assembly consider CA.7a Integral normal bases and trace (retained targets through Hilbert–Speiser), CA.7b Orders and stable modules (K₀, Steinitz, ideles, rank-one classes, Eichler cancellation), CA.7c Character determinants and tame obstruction (Hom quotient, Gauss sums, logarithm, Fröhlich–Taylor). Keep the current single stage until the manager approves this split. Each block has at most six named planets. If CA.7 remains unsplit, select a combined six-planet palette: Normal integral basis, Noether theorem, Hilbert–Speiser theorem, Locally free class group, Jacobinski cancellation, Fröhlich–Taylor theorem; the six continuation markers are not six extra planets to append to the inherited palette.

Proposals of this assembly:

17. **Atlas edges should follow the targets.** The stage list of the atlas still draws ArithmeticDynamics DY.1 → CA.6 and KTheoryLowDegrees Z.1 → CA.7. The plan no longer cites either: those notions moved down, so DY.1 and Z.1, Z.4 import from CA.6 and CA.7. It also still draws the retired FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration LI.0, LI.1, LI.3 and LI.4, whose content the targets cite directly from the libraries and from Class Field Theory. The targets themselves cite the following:

- lower tiers: DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence DT.0 → CA.6 and DT.2 → CA.2; GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.1, GN.3 and GN.4 → CA.4, and GN.2 → CA.7; IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0 → CA.7; AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.4 → CA.7;
- inside the roadmap: CA.2 → CA.3, CA.2 → CA.6, CA.3 → CA.4, CA.3 → CA.5, CA.4 → CA.5 and CA.5 → CA.3 (one target, below).

No target cites CA.0 from CA.1 or CA.2, CA.1 from CA.4, CA.3 or CA.5 from CA.6, or CA.5 from CA.7. Those stage requirements describe the intended reading order, not dependencies.

18. **Move the index of ℤ[√d] into CA.3.** `CA.3/imaginary-quadratic-polya-fields` cites `CA.5/index-of-the-order-z-sqrt-d`, and CA.5 cites nine CA.3 targets, so the layers cite each other. The index target needs only Tau Ceti's integral-primitive-element index and the quadratic discriminants. The package should state it in CA.3, before the Pólya fields, with CA.5 citing it there; its packet id need not change before then.

19. **Adopt the proposed sub-layers.** The sub-layer proposals of CA.1 (three), CA.2 (four), CA.3 (three), CA.4 (five) and CA.7 (three blocks, or the IntegralGaloisModuleStructure split) each give at most six planets per sub-layer. The assembly removed planets so that each layer shows six; once sub-layers exist, the removed planets can be restored. They are listed in the packets' `assemblyEdits`.

## Notes for Tau Ceti roadmaps and for the libraries

These are recorded for the maintainer to pass on; no Tau Ceti roadmap is re-planned here.

- **EllipticCurves, Layer 1, milestone (iv).** It states Ê(𝔪) ≅ E₁(K) for an integral model, which is what elliptic divisibility sequences need. The finer filtration E_k(K) = {O} ∪ {v(x) ≤ −2k}, with E_k/E_{k+1} ≅ k⁺, is not named in that roadmap; CA.2 plans it for an arbitrary integral equation. If Layer 4 states its reduction filtration only for a minimal equation, it should remark that E₁ of a nonminimal integral equation is the image of that equation's own formal group, not the kernel of reduction of the minimal model.
- **Class Field Theory, Layer 5.** `h2MuEquivZMod_mixed` asserts only that some coordinate of H²(F, μ_n) exists. CA.1's comparison of the norm-residue symbol with localSymbol fixes it as the invariant coordinate and requests that choice. The universal sign ε is then a computation once the sign conventions of `kummerClass` and of the cup product are fixed.
- **The current Tau Ceti library**, newer than the pin, was screened by the CA.7 continuation. It found the following:
  - The restriction functor on G₀ acts on finite modules, not on projective K₀.
  - The ring-equivalence compatibility of projective K₀ does not give arbitrary scalar maps.
  - The local orbit lattice of the normal basis is not a full normal integral basis of a tame ring of integers.
  - Nothing supplies a generic reduced norm, a Steinitz comparison or an integral group logarithm.

  The CA.5 continuation found NumberFieldArithmetic's unit-candidate certificates and the golden-ratio unit and regulator theorems there. They are imported as examples.
- **For the package of this roadmap.** The package of DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence predates `DT.0/siegel-lemma-number-field-product`, the product form of Siegel's lemma that `CA.6/dobrowolski-auxiliary-polynomial` uses. This roadmap's package must therefore cite a DT layer that contains it, or state the lemma.
- **For ComputationalNumberTheory CN.2.** It should cite `tauceti:TauCeti.kernelBasis` and `tauceti:TauCeti.freeColumnBasis` directly. It should import CA.5's four soundness criteria rather than restating them: its nodes `units-complete-of-regulator-bound`, `joint-class-unit-index-certificate` and `certified-class-unit-completeness` restate CA.5 targets.

Every source the targets cite, by identifier, with its edition and public link. All were read in public copies or, for Platonov–Rapinchuk–Rapinchuk, from the maintainer-cleared library. ## The suggested Lean file

[`ClassicalArithmeticCompletion.lean`](../suggested/ClassicalArithmeticCompletion.lean) joins the suggested files of the first pass and of the seven continuations. It has one import block of 188 individual Mathlib and Tau Ceti modules and one standard note, and every declaration is in the namespace `TauCeti.ClassicalArithmetic`. Each layer has the first-pass section, then a section `CAkContinuation` with the continuation's statements. The first pass's Cobham section sits with CA.2, and its order-to-unit comparison for d ≡ 1 (mod 4) with CA.5. The file elaborates with `lean-check` at Mathlib `082e2d3` and Tau Ceti `f790474`. Every warning is for an admitted proof.

Reconciliations made in the join:

- **Duplicates removed.** The continuations restated first-pass declarations so that each could elaborate on its own. Only the first-pass copies are kept:
  - from the CA.1 continuation: `normEquationSymbol`, `ratSquarefreePart`, `powerResidueSymbol`, `powerResidueSymbolIdeal`, `IsPrimaryEisenstein` and `IsEisensteinPrimary`, together with the promoted API items `ratSquarefreePart_mul_sq`, `prime_dvd_ratSquarefreePart_iff`, `isPrimaryEisenstein_add_mul_iff` and `exists_unique_associated_isPrimaryEisenstein`;
  - from the CA.3 continuation: `intValuedPolynomials` and `characteristicIdeal`;
  - from the CA.4 continuation: `markoffSet`, `markoffVieta`, `positiveMarkoffTriples` and `pellNormSet`.

  A comment at each removal names the declaration that stays.
- **One form of the determinant criterion.** The general `relationDet_eq_classNumber_iff` of the CA.5 continuation, for any surjection onto the class group, is kept. The first pass's `natAbs_det_eq_classNumber_iff` is the same statement for the presentation map of an ideal family, whose kernel is `relationLattice I`. It is named in a comment.
- **One norm convention.** The negative Pell comparisons use `Algebra.norm ℤ` on 𝓞_K, as the first pass does; the CA.5 continuation had `Algebra.norm ℚ` on K in one statement.
- **One namespace.** The CA.5, CA.6 and CA.7 continuations had their own namespaces (`…CA5`, `TauCeti.MahlerAnalytic`, `…CA7Continuation`). Their packets' `library` namespaces now agree with the file.
- **Scopes.**
  - The first pass defines local namespaces `TauCeti.ClassicalArithmetic.Polynomial` and `TauCeti.ClassicalArithmetic.PowerSeries`, so an `open` of either inside the namespace names `_root_` explicitly.
  - The CA.2 continuation imports Mathlib's Bernoulli polynomials, so the first pass's `bernoulli` is written `_root_.bernoulli`.
  - Each section is closed where it ends.

Eighteen definitions inherited from the part files have admitted bodies: seventeen from the first pass and `stickelbergerPhi` from the CA.1 continuation. Most are constructions whose algorithm or equivalence is itself a target, such as the Smith and Hermite forms, the structure of (ℤ/2^k)ˣ, the p-adic digit equivalence and the class-group equivalences. `scripts/check_sorry_data.py` also lists three in the first pass's commented-out CA.7 interfaces for the locally free class group, which are not elaborated. The package keeps real bodies only, as `PACKAGE_REVIEW.md` requires.

The file closes with a list, by target, of the 226 names that the packets propose for API items, unit tests and declarations of 33 targets but that the file does not type. The CA.6 and CA.7 continuations stated their analytic and K-theoretic carriers in the document only, since those carriers are not at the pins.
